evidence: Source review against native build 1: existing Ticket, conversation, artifact, error, and update response shapes remain readable. The optional machine_id health query preserves the original executor response when omitted, as APIClient.executorHealth does today. Destination-specific health is available in the web interface; native build 1 still reads the original executor health and does not expose the new selection. Legacy vps/macos aliases remain for the original destinations. Machine credentials and protocol 26 protect executor routes, which the native APIClient does not call. Executor reads now check the dispatched URL path before any file route can run. Shared Ticket reads retain existing agent permissions. The original executor transition keeps one recoverable pending credential until its first authenticated request, then permanently closes old authority. This changes executor authentication rather than native owner authentication. The runtime connection pool preserves native database transactions and commit participants. The retained cache matches existing request-worker concurrency. Exhausted retained slots use temporary connections without a pool wait. Cleanup preserves the original operation error. Existing API response shapes and native owner authentication remain unchanged. The default health response retains _with_native_build_1_fields. The native build floor, draft/outbox code, reconnect paths, and APNs payload are unchanged. Focused source review, destination health HTTP coverage, and Svelte checks support retaining build 1 for its retained interface. Signed-device, TestFlight, native destination-specific UI, reconnect, and draft-survival behavior are not tested. This is a source compatibility receipt, not device or release readiness. Final source, migration, and native-context fixture checks retain their original assertions with machine ownership and foreign keys active. Combined Mac home review: APIClient.deployment, DeploymentStatus, and DeploymentStrip retain deployment response shapes. The native APIClient does not call /api/updates or decode its Darwin runtime contract. The home uses a Python runtime and retains the authoritative idle check and atomic admission claim after its waiting-poll scheduling repair. Linux Node admission and exact-schema restrictions remain intact. The Mac snapshot remains mandatory across the added migrations. Runtime and registry shutdown precede connection-pool closure, before the independent installer restores records offline. Private ICU packaging preserves the macOS 15 floor. No native build-floor change follows from the combined source. Native startup, update, and unhealthy rollback on this combined tree remain a separate disposable proof, not a signed-device proof. The final completion wake rechecks waiting updates after admitted work drains, without changing the authoritative idle check, atomic claim, or API fields. Owner shutdown invalidates queued callbacks before cleanup. SIGUSR1 thread diagnostics stay inside the Python application and its existing stderr log. Neither change alters retained native decoding or the minimum build policy. Installed-layout no-repository tests cover both authenticated and rejected service identities. This source review still does not establish device or native release-trial readiness. Run 12 follow-up source review: fixed Mac release job executable paths and Python bytecode suppression change process environments and launcher flags only. The idle/confirmed Update now policy remains shared by Linux and Darwin. No HTTP field, native model, authentication policy, or build floor changes. The source review retains native build 1. Local process tests cover both sealed launchers and the Darwin application child. Signed-device and TestFlight behavior remain not tested. The managed-launcher integration fixture recognizes -B while retaining its environment and owner-configuration assertions.
